title: X0 hardware gate (Qwen3.6-27B, 2x H100 box): does the new box reproduce one 23 Oct necessity cell?
command: uv run python scripts/statement_positions.py parts --name x0_hw_gate_parts_27b --map d1_topics2_map_27b --why "X0 hardware gate: one 23 Oct cell (bridge_word:16) rerun on the 2x H100 box" --lo 16 --sets bridge_word --force bridge_word:16 && uv run python scripts/x0_hw_gate.py --new x0_hw_gate_parts_27b --ref d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2 --cell bridge_word:16
question: Does the new box (2x H100 80GB PCIe, x86_64, driver CUDA 12.8) reproduce, read for read, a cell the 23 Oct necessity run (d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2, A100) measured: the bridge's word at layer 16, both readers, the same scenes, map, lens and code path?
why_it_matters: X0 compares its numbers with the 23 Oct ones and is the gate for the week. A hardware or kernel difference that flips reads would be confounded with the effect.

hypotheses.H-same: the reads agree on >= 97% of rows without random draws. Prior: none set (an agreement check, not a claim)
hypotheses.H-differs: the agreement is below 97%: X0 does not start; the disagreeing rows are reported

decision_rule: Fixed 24 Oct before the run (hardware addendum v2: "rerun one 23 Oct cell, item agreement at least 97%"). Rows are matched on item, set, layer, part, source and null flag (scripts/x0_hw_gate.py). The gate covers the rows whose arm draws no random tensor: full, lens2, not_lens2, jspace, not_jspace, jspace_wo_own and not_jspace_matched, non-null, both readers. PASS iff the share of those rows whose read role (b / A / other) matches the 23 Oct row is >= 0.97. Otherwise FAIL: the script exits 3, so the X0 jobs that depend on this one do not start. Arms drawing random tensors (rand_omp, rand_sub, not_rand_sub, the matched pieces, every null; drawn on CUDA in this code) are reported per part, not gated. The median |ld| difference is reported per group.
controls: the reference run itself: the same code path (statement_positions.py, exp04_brew_parts.py, suite_split.py, tasks_v2.py, suite_v1.py and src/bridge_jspace/ have no diff between c2e31c9, the reference run's commit, and this commit)
the random-draw arms reported beside the gate
n: 180 scenes x 2 readers (PP, PM) of d1_topics_v2, one cell (bridge_word:16), 7784 rows in the reference
notes: The reference ran on the A100 box at c2e31c9 (dirty tree; the parts code path has no diff since). Inputs are committed: results/statement_positions/d1_topics2_map_27b, results/tasks_v2/d1_topics2_competence_27b, results/statement_positions/d1_necessity_parts_27b_r2. GPU0, first job of the queue (hardware addendum v2). Timing basis: the reference's 8 cells took ~1.3 h on one A100; one cell is ~10 min.

title: X0, Qwen3.5-9B, chat (decisive) and raw: is C3's split real at layer 12, and is it about J++?
command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b uv run python scripts/x0_necessity.py run --name x0_necessity_9b --set d1_topics_v3 --renderings chat raw --why "X0 (jobs/c3/X0.md, amendment 1): the 9B, chat (decisive) and raw; bridge word, layers 6-20 every 2, predicted 12"
figures_command: BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b uv run python scripts/x0_necessity.py figures --name x0_necessity_9b
question: On fresh scenes (d1_topics_v3, seed 24), at the bridge's word of the 9B: past layer 12 (fixed in advance), does removing the J++-readable part of a stated bridge's change stop hurting lookups (no more than a random part of the same share) while it still hurts recalls, with the chat template and in raw text? And does W_U, W_E or a random dictionary do the same as J++?
why_it_matters: C3's pre-registered confirmation on the second model, and the stop rule for X1-X4 on the 9B (D3: per model). The raw arm answers whether the split depends on the chat template.

hypotheses.H-confirmed: lookup excess <= 0.10 and recall Jdep >= 0.30 at layer 12 (chat, J++, top-token read). Prior: Dan's, predictions/2026-10-24_dan.md Q25.4
hypotheses.H-killed: lookup excess >= 0.20 or recall Jdep < 0.20 at layer 12. Prior: Dan's, Q25.4
hypotheses.H-not-confirmed: neither of the above. Prior: Dan's, Q25.4
hypotheses.H-raw-same: raw passes the gate and gets the chat verdict. Prior: Dan's, Q25.1 and Q25.5
hypotheses.H-token: W_E's lookup excess >= 0.20 (against W_E's own random part) while J++ leaves the lookup around. Prior: Dan's, Q25.7

decision_rule: jobs/c3/X0.md "Decision rule" with amendment 1 (24 Oct, before data), on this run's chat rendering at layer 12: confirmed iff lookup excess <= 0.10 and recall Jdep >= 0.30 (23 Oct); killed iff lookup excess >= 0.20 or recall Jdep < 0.20 (24 Oct); not confirmed otherwise (24 Oct); can't tell if either reader's cell is invalid (S_whole < 0.30 or < 30 items switched; 24 Oct). Point estimates, top-token read (raw: the first non-whitespace token); cand read descriptive. Raw is reported beside chat with the same rule and labels; a raw gate failure is "can't test". Not opened before Dan's batch-25 answers are committed.
controls: the random part of the same share, per dictionary (no_rand_D, at D's own share of ||Δ||²)
the random Gaussian dictionary at k = 25 (the fitted null, rand_omp)
both readers on the identical patch
the valid-cell bar on the whole edit (S_whole >= 0.30 and >= 30 items)
the competence gate per rendering (>= 80% unedited org accuracy under the decisive read, both readers)
the asked-first subset (D5, descriptive)
n: up to 200 eligible scenes of d1_topics_v3 (600 generated) per rendering, 2 readers each; < 150 eligible = can't test
notes: Seeds: data 24 (d1_topics_v3), random dictionary 777 + layer and random subspace 888 + layer (CPU), bootstrap 0 (10,000), examples 0. Lens: the 9B's pinned J++ (sha256 checked on load). Not gated by a 9B hardware check: x0_hw_gate_27b passed on this box (0.9898) for the same code path; the 9B's 23 Oct rows are a different read and set. Timing basis: qwen35_9b_d1_topics2_parts, 23k reads in 852 s on an A100; this job ~ 200 x 2 x (8 x 9 + 15) x 2 renderings ~ 70k reads, raw up to ~2 forwards per arm: ~0.5-0.7 h. Dan, 24 Oct: run now; results not opened until his batch-25 answers are committed.
